title: How to Experience the Scenic Blue Train Without the Crowds
excerpt: Securing first-class observation salon tickets and selecting the optimal scenic segment between Nanu Oya and Ella for unobstructed panoramic views.

cover.alt: Blue hill country train crossing the Nine Arches Bridge amid tea plantations

content:
The hill-country railway from Kandy to Ella is one of the great train journeys of the world: tunnels, waterfalls, tea estates rolling away on both sides and stations that have barely changed since the 1920s. It is also, in high season, one of the busiest. With a little planning, it can still feel like the romantic journey it should be.

## Choose the right segment

The full line from Kandy to Ella takes six to seven hours. It is beautiful, but long, and the most spectacular scenery is concentrated in the second half. For most guests I recommend boarding at **Nanu Oya** (the station for Nuwara Eliya) and riding to **Ella**: about three and a half hours through the highest and most dramatic part of the line, including the summit at Pattipola and the descent through Haputale's cloud forest.

### When the long version makes sense

If you love trains, or if you are travelling as a couple with nowhere else to be, the full journey from Kandy (or Peradeniya) is a day to remember. I pack a picnic lunch and your luggage travels ahead by car.

## Which class to book

- **First-class observation saloon:** a carriage at the end of the train with a large rear window. Seats are reserved and air-conditioned on some services, but the windows do not open.
- **Second class reserved:** my personal favourite. Open windows, fresh mountain air, a reserved seat — and the famous doorway views.
- **Third class:** lively and fun for a short stretch, but unreserved and often very crowded.

## How tickets really work

Reserved seats open thirty days before the travel date and sell out within minutes in the dry season. They are allocated to a limited number of carriages, and online platforms often show "sold out" while foreign travellers pay agents inflated prices for the same seats.

For my guests, I book the allocation directly through station contacts as soon as reservations open and confirm the coach and seat numbers in your itinerary. If the train you want is full, I suggest a different departure rather than a crowded unreserved carriage.

## Avoiding the crowds on board

1. **Take the early train.** The morning departures are quieter and the light over the tea is softer.
2. **Sit on the right side going to Ella.** Most of the valley views open on the right-hand side between Nanu Oya and Haputale.
3. **Travel mid-week.** Weekends and school holidays bring local families heading to the hills.
4. **Send your luggage by car.** Large suitcases fill the aisles. With a private vehicle following the line, you board with a day bag only.

## Seeing the Nine Arches Bridge

The Nine Arches viaduct near Ella is best seen from the ground rather than from the train. I take guests to a quiet tea terrace with a clear view of the bridge and check the day's train times, so we arrive just before a crossing instead of waiting on the crowded embankment.

## Safety on the doorstep

The doorway photos are famous, but trains lurch on curves and tunnels come quickly. Hold the rail, keep your feet inside the carriage and step back in the tunnels. I would rather you remember the journey than the photograph.

If the scenic train is on your wish list, [tell me when you would like to travel](/contact) and I will secure the right seats on the right day.
